places.name: Blue Lagoon

note.why_go: A milky-blue geothermal lagoon in a black lava field on the Reykjanes peninsula, 20 km from Keflavík airport: Iceland's best-known bath.
note.best_time: First slot of the day or the evening; on the way to or from the airport
note.crowd_hint: Entry is by timed ticket and sells out: book days ahead
note.etiquette: Shower without a swimsuit before bathing. Eruptions nearby have closed it at short notice: check on the day.

places.why: Iceland's most visited sight lay 5 km west of the destination's box. The box now takes in the Reykjanes peninsula, so the lagoon is an ordinary place of the destination: must-see and the fifteenth essential.

places.name: Keflavík International Airport

note.why_go: Iceland's international airport, 50 km south-west of Reykjavík; the Flybus coach to Reykjavík runs in connection with every flight.
note.best_time: Allow 45 minutes by road from Reykjavík
note.crowd_hint: Busiest in the early-morning and mid-afternoon flight banks

places.why: Visitors land here, and it lay outside the box. The recommended record of the airport was pinned at the BSÍ bus terminal in Reykjavík (batch 02 lists it to hide); this is the airport itself. Recommended, not a must-see.

places.name: Teotihuacán

note.why_go: The ruined city of Teotihuacán, 50 km north-east: the Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon along the 2 km Avenue of the Dead. A half-day trip.
note.best_time: At opening (8:00): there is almost no shade and it is hot by midday
note.crowd_hint: Tour groups arrive from 9:30; Sundays are the busiest
note.etiquette: Carry water, a hat and sunscreen. Climb only where it is open (in 2026 the Moon's first platform).

places.why: The day trip most first visits make lay 10 km beyond the box. The box now reaches it, so the site is an ordinary place of the destination: must-see and essential. One place, not three: the pyramids and the avenue are one ticket and one walk, and a plan reads better with one stop of three and a half hours than with three stops a few hundred metres apart. Opening hours, the midday heat and the climbing rule are from Wikivoyage's Teotihuacán guide (read 5 October 2026).

checked.source: OpenStreetMap way 251373335 “Pirámide del Sol” (historic=ruins); the record sits on the Avenue of the Dead beside it

places.why: A proposal, for the controller to decide: Mexico City holds 15 essentials, the most allowed, and Teotihuacán becomes one. This garden gives way: it is a 30-minute stop, the shortest of the fifteen, and Coyoacán keeps an essential 700 m away in the Frida Kahlo Museum. It stays a must-see. The other candidates were Torre Latinoamericana (a viewing deck beside Bellas Artes) and La Ciudadela Craft Market (the only market among the essentials, which is why it was kept).
